## agent-ml-research
ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

- mvp-001 (Qwen-rewrite) 定位为 "pilot study demonstrating feasibility"，后续用 continuation mode rigorously validate
- cont→rw 89% vs rw→cont 82% 不对称性 → continuation features 是 rewrite 的通用子集

## Core Claims (2+1 结构, D012)

### Primary: C1' (K* Characterization)
首次系统测量递归合成文本的 generational discrimination boundary K*，并揭示其 universality。

DPI 理论证明有限 K*_theory 必然存在（信息论 impossibility boundary）；我们首次在受控实验中测量 K*_empirical，它提供 K*_theory 的保守下界。通过 8 条件实验矩阵（4 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies）系统表征 K*_empirical 的行为，发现 K*=2 在所有 8 个测试条件下保持不变，展现出跨模型架构、跨解码策略、跨生成模式的 universality。

**子组件：**

**(a) K*=2 universality across architectures, generation modes, and decoding strategies**
> **4/4 model-mode configurations 与 4/4 decoding strategies 全部 K*=2：**
>
> *Model × mode (exp-007):*
> | Model | AUC 1v2 | 95% CI | CI lower > 0.60? |
> |-------|---------|--------|-----------------|
> | Qwen-rewrite | 0.6955 | [0.6859, 0.7041] | ✅ (+8.6pp) |
> | Pythia-1.4B | 0.6539 | [0.6454, 0.6630] | ✅ (+4.5pp) |
> | OLMo-1B | 0.6145 | [0.6045, 0.6247] | ✅ (+0.45pp) |
> | Qwen-cont | 0.6112 | [0.6015, 0.6213] | ✅ (+0.15pp, 最边缘) |
>
> *Decoding strategy invariance (exp-003):*
> | Decoding | AUC 1v2 | K* |
> |----------|---------|-----|
> | greedy | 0.6893 | 2 |
> | nucleus p=0.9 | 0.6866 | 2 |
> | temp=0.7 | 0.6887 | 2 |
> | temp=1.2 | 0.7039 | 2 |
>
> - 全部 1v2 CI lower > 0.60, 全部 2v3 CI upper < 0.60, 全部 permutation p < 0.002
> - 4 decoding strategies 的 AUC 1v2 range [0.6866, 0.7039]，K* 完全不变
> - K*=2 在所有 8 个测试条件下保持不变（4 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies）
> - ⚠️ θ-sensitivity: θ=0.60 下 4/4 K*=2；θ=0.70 下仅 Config4-T12 K*=2（1v2=0.7039 仅超 0.70 阈值 0.004），其余 3 config K*=1。论文以 θ=0.60 为主结论，θ=0.70 边界效应作 footnote
> - ⚠️ 特征排序分化: K* 跨 config 稳定，但特征重要性排序不完全一致——Greedy vs T1.2 Spearman=0.53, p=0.041（Bonferroni 校正后阈值 0.0083，不显著）。论文中措辞应为 "suggestive" 而非确定性结论。Config4-T12 正确 top-3 features: hapax_ratio, ttr, surp_skew（非 freq_entropy）
> - ⚠️ K*=2 边缘性双端注意: Qwen-cont 1v2 CI lower=0.6015（+0.15pp 高于 θ）+ Qwen-rw 2v3 CI upper=0.5991（-0.09pp 低于 θ），K*=2 边界在两端都极边缘。Discussion/Limitations 需同时提及
> - Paper 可写："K*=2 is established as a consistent discrimination boundary across all 8 tested conditions (4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies; bootstrap 95% CI for AUC₁ᵥ₂ > 0.60; AUC₂ᵥ₃ CI upper < 0.60), suggesting universality beyond the ≤1.5B scale studied."
> - ⚠️ 措辞策略（D017 Reviewer 评估）：分两层——"established as consistent" 用确定性语言（8/8 有统计检验支撑），"suggesting universality beyond" 对外推 hedging。不升级为 "establishing universal"——3 模型 ≤1.5B 会引发审稿人质疑消耗 rebuttal 预算
> - ⚠️ C1' 子组件定位：呈现为"对同一 claim 的 4 个 evidence 维度"而非 4 个独立 finding。§4 标题用 "K* Characterization"，每个子节开头显式回答一个 reviewer concern，子节间用 transitional sentences 链接

**(b) Cross-model transfer**
> - Pythia↔OLMo 90-92% accuracy retention → K*=2 不是 model self-familiarity artifact
> - 0v1 AUC > 0.96 across all transfer pairs → binary contamination signal 完全跨模型可迁移
> - 1v2+ transfer 取决于模型族相似度 → 与 K*=2 完美一致（K* 之上分辨力本就微弱）
> - transfer retention 80-92% suggests depth signal has a large text-intrinsic component（不量化具体比例，因 transfer accuracy retention ≠ 信号分解）
> - ⚠️ 数值精度：Pythia→OLMo 91.6%, OLMo→Pythia 90.3%，范围 90-92%（非 91-92%）；Qwen-cont↔Pythia 84.7%/85.2%，范围 84-85%（非 83-85%）

**(c) Degradation ordering consistency**
> - Spearman ρ ≥ 0.85 on single-feature AUC ranking（mode-controlled, continuation）
> - Top discriminative features shared: surp_d1_std, surp_std, surp_d2_std
> - Limitation: depth-pair level 一致性在 1v2 处较弱（τ~0.37）
> - Metric: single-feature AUC ranking（model-free, not LightGBM split count）

**(e) Representation dependence of K* (§4.x Neural Probe / §5.x Discussion)**
> - exp-015 完整 3 模型结果（frozen self-embeddings + MLP probe, each model probing its own generations）:
>   - Qwen-cont: K*(neural)=3, 2v3 AUC=0.6159, CI [0.6099, 0.6223], CI lower > 0.60 ✅
>   - Pythia-1.4B: K*(neural)=2, 2v3 AUC=0.5963, CI [0.5892, 0.6033], CI lower < 0.60 ❌
>   - OLMo-1B: K*(neural)=2, 2v3 AUC=0.5892, CI [0.5818, 0.5965], CI lower < 0.60 ❌
> - **K*(neural) 不具备 universality**：仅 Qwen-cont 达到 K*=3，Pythia/OLMo 仍为 K*=2
> - **Self-familiarity 解释**：每个模型用自己的 frozen embeddings 探测自己生成的文本。Qwen 对 Qwen-generated 文本更敏感（self-familiarity），K*=3 是 model-specific artifact 而非 universal signal
> - **K*(theory) ≥ 3 弱化**：只能 claim "K*(theory) ≥ 3 for Qwen representations"，不能泛化为所有模型
> - **Interpretability–deployability tradeoff 加强**：15D features 给出 universal K*=2（3/3 模型一致），neural probe 给出 model-dependent K*∈{2,3}。Model-free 方案的 universality 优势在 cross-model 结果下更明显
> - 所有 3 模型 neural 2v3 AUC > lgbm 2v3 AUC（+3.9pp 到 +5.5pp），说明 learned representations 确实恢复了额外 depth signal，但不足以在所有模型上推过 θ=0.60
> - 论文定位：**正面发现**——cross-model validation 揭示 K*(neural) 是 representation-dependent，验证了选择 model-free 15D features 作为 headline K* characterization 的正确性
> - 预防审稿人 "why bury the stronger result?"：K*(neural)=3 仅对 Qwen 成立且是 self-familiarity driven，不适合作为 headline result；15D K*=2 的 universality（8/8 conditions + 3/3 models）才是可靠可部署的结论

**(d) Generation mode analysis (§4.x Analysis subsection)**
> - Signal strength: rewrite AUC 1v2=0.6957 vs continuation 0.6114（Δ=+8.4pp）
> - Transferability: continuation 80-92% retention vs rewrite 61-63%
> - Feature subset: cont→rw 89% > rw→cont 82% → continuation features 是 rewrite 的通用子集
> - Interpretation: rewrite mode 的 instruction-following 引入 mode-specific style artifacts，放大 depth signal 但降低跨模型泛化性
> - 论文定位：Analysis subsection（"How does generation mode affect depth estimation?"），不是独立 claim

### Secondary: C3 (K*-Aware Data Curation Validation)
K*=2 correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit: binary K*-aware filtering (0.5941 MMLU) outperforms graduated depth weighting (best 0.5892 at α=0.9), surprisal-based selection (0.5894), and DSIR distribution matching (~0.5867, ≈ no-filter level). K* serves as an actionable curation guideline — the discrimination boundary directly determines the optimal filtering granularity.

### Supporting Analysis: Canonical Condition Selection
Generation mode 是 depth estimation 的显著混淆变量。Methodology 段落阐述 continuation mode 作为 canonical condition 的选择及理由（不作为独立 claim）。

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: Web 数据正被多代递归合成文本污染。当前检测方法将合成文本视为 binary 类别（real vs synthetic），但质量随代际深度非线性退化——首代合成文本与四代合成文本的质量差异巨大却被忽视。
- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (DivEye, Min-K%++) 不区分代际；model collapse 文献 (Shumailov et al., Alemohammad et al. 2024, Dohmatob et al. 2024) 描述宏观现象但不提供检测工具；data selection methods (DSIR, D4, DoReMi) 做分布匹配但不估计递归深度；Drayson et al. (2025) 将 binary MGT detection 应用于 importance resampling 以防止 model collapse，是目前最接近的工作。然而这些方法均做二值判断，**不估计文本经历了多少轮递归生成，也不量化辨别能力的饱和边界。**
- **Our framing**: 将递归生成建模为 iterated lossy channel，从信息论（DPI）推导出 K* 的必然存在。K* 是首次系统测量的 operational quantity——它告诉数据策展者"在什么深度以下，depth-aware curation 比 binary detection 更有价值"。通过 8 条件实验矩阵（4 model-mode configurations + 4 decoding strategies）系统表征 K*，揭示其 universality：**K*=2 在所有测试条件下不变**，表明递归生成存在一个与具体模型架构和解码策略无关的 universal discrimination boundary。这一发现为数据治理提供 actionable guidance——depth-aware filtering 在 K* 以内有效，且无需针对不同模型或解码配置分别调优。
- **Headline result template**: "Recursive generation has a universal discrimination boundary at K*=2: invariant across 4 model-mode configurations and 4 decoding strategies (8 conditions total) at ≤1.5B scale, with cross-model transfer retention of 80-92% confirming depth features are largely text-intrinsic. K*=2 correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit — binary filtering at K* (0.5941 MMLU) outperforms all tested alternatives including graduated weighting, surprisal selection, and DSIR."

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Responses

1. **"Universality claim 只基于 ≤1.5B 模型，能推广到更大模型吗？"** → 这是最大 limitation，论文明确标注 "at ≤1.5B scale"；但 (i) universality 在 4 个不同架构族（GPT-2 style, Pythia, OLMo, Qwen）间已成立，说明不是单一架构的 artifact；(ii) DPI 理论保证 K*_theory 对任意规模模型存在，实证 K*_empirical 在更大模型上可能更大（信号更丰富）也可能不变（lossy channel 特性稳定），这是重要的 future work
2. **"只是 feature engineering + off-the-shelf classifier，方法贡献弱"** → 贡献在 problem formulation + empirical characterization（首次测量 K*）+ 理论框架（DPI）+ universality 发现，不是分类器本身
3. **"Prompt-chain 不代表真实世界递归污染"** → retrain-chain ecological validity check 作为补充；prompt-chain 是 controlled experiment 的标准方法
4. **"K*=2 太浅，graduated filtering 收益有限"** → K*=2 恰好预测了这一结果：binary filtering at K* boundary (0.5941 MMLU) outperforms graduated weighting (best 0.5892), surprisal selection (0.5894), and DSIR (~0.5867). 这验证了 K* 作为 actionable curation guideline 的价值——discrimination boundary 直接决定了最优 filtering 粒度。K* 的 universality 意味着实践者无需为每个模型/解码配置单独标定阈值
5. **"同模型做生成和 surprisal 计算有 bias"** → **exp-013 直接反驳**：Pythia↔OLMo 90-92% accuracy retention，0v1 transfer AUC > 0.96。Depth signal 主要编码在文本而非 model self-familiarity
6. **"为什么不用 learned representations"** → **exp-015 直接回应**：frozen LLM embeddings + MLP probe 达到 K*=3（vs 15D K*=2），揭示 representation-dependent hierarchy: K*_theory ≥ K*_neural ≥ K*_15D。Hand-crafted 15D features 的优势在于 model-free transferability（80-92% cross-model retention）、可解释性（支持 degradation ordering 分析）、实用可部署性。Neural representations 多辨别 1 个深度级别但代价是 model dependence + ~100x 计算开销。这一 tradeoff 证明 15D features 是 practical choice，同时表明 theoretical boundary 延伸至 K*=2 之上
7. **"Graduated filtering 没和 data selection methods 比"** → exp-006 包含 DSIR baseline + α sensitivity sweep
8. **"Decoding strategy 只测了 4 种，coverage 不够"** → 覆盖了实践中最常见的 decoding 配置（greedy, nucleus sampling, temperature scaling high/low）；4/4 完全一致强化 universality claim；extreme decoding（top-k=1 之外的 pathological 配置）留作 future work
9. **"为什么不直接用 LLM 做 depth estimation"** → **exp-011 直接反驳**：GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.6 在 500 样本 zero-shot 5-class depth 分类上仅 33.1-33.2% accuracy（MAE ~1.1），低于 OBD 15-feature LightGBM 的 38.6%。二者 binary detection 均 ~88%，说明 LLM 能区分 human vs synthetic 但无法估计递归深度。depth estimation 是非平凡任务，需要专用特征工程

## Venue Fit

- EMNLP 2026 special theme 明确呼吁 data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance 方向的工作
- 2+1 claim 结构：C1' 是 comprehensive characterization study with universality finding，C3 是 practical application，generation mode analysis 增加深度
- Universality narrative 比 controllability 更有 impact：从 "K* depends on X, Y, Z" 升级为 "K*=2 is a universal boundary"，审稿人更容易记住和传播
- 风险：universality claim 在 ≤1.5B 规模下的外推性是最大攻击面 → 论文中 scope 明确、limitation 诚实、DPI 理论支撑泛化的合理性

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When models train on the outputs of earlier models, the resulting multi-generational synthetic text degrades with each iteration: tail modes vanish, lexical diversity contracts, and surprisal distributions flatten~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively generating from previous outputs without retraining); we study the latter, which isolates generation-level information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically, discarding the generational depth dimension.

The gap cuts across three communities.
Binary detection methods~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp, zawalski2026codec} produce no depth estimate.
The model collapse literature~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, schaeffer2025position} characterizes recursive degradation at the macro level but provides no per-text depth estimation tool.
Data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} ignore recursive depth.
No existing method estimates how many rounds of recursive generation a text has undergone, nor quantifies the boundary beyond which such estimation becomes infeasible.

The Data Processing Inequality guarantees that information degrades monotonically across generations, motivating a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$.
We empirically measure $\Kempirical$---the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations---using 15 statistical features and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k$ where the bootstrap 95\% CI for pairwise $\auc_{k,k+1}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$.

Our primary contribution is a systematic empirical characterization of $\Kempirical$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{$\Kempirical = 2$ at $\theta{=}0.60$} (Cohen's $h{\approx}0.20$) across 4 model-mode configurations (Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}) and a decoding strategy ablation on Qwen-rewrite covering 4 strategies (Table~\ref{tab:s2_decoding}), with all 1v2 CI lower bounds exceeding $\theta$ and all 2v3 CI upper bounds below $\theta$ (permutation $p \leq 0.002$).
  \item \textbf{Cross-model transfer}: 80--92\% accuracy retention across continuation-mode generators; 0v1 $\auc > 0.96$ (range: 0.963--0.991) across all pairs.
  \item \textbf{Feature degradation consistency}: Spearman $\rho \geq 0.85$ on single-feature rankings across continuation-mode models, with surprisal-variance features dominating.
  \item \textbf{Generation mode}: rewrite yields higher 1v2 $\auc$ ($+$8.4\,pp) but transfers poorly (61--63\% vs.\ 80--92\%).
\end{enumerate}

\noindent As a secondary contribution, $\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts the strategy ordering in downstream filtering: binary curation at the $\Kempirical$ boundary minimizes degradation most effectively (MMLU $0.5941$ vs.\ base $0.6018$), while graduated ($0.5892$) and surprisal-based ($0.5894$) strategies provide no additional benefit (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).

1	\section{Application: $\Kstar$-Aware Data Filtering}
2	\label{sec:filtering}
3	
4	$\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit over binary filtering.
5	We compare six data curation strategies on a corpus of 30{,}000 documents (5{,}000 per depth, depths 0--5): (i)~\textbf{no-filter} (uniform weight), (ii)~\textbf{binary-ours} ($w = 1 - P(\text{synthetic})$ from the 15D LightGBM classifier), (iii)~\textbf{binary-Drayson} (importance weighting following \citet{drayson2025}, same classifier, weights $w_j \propto (1 - q(x_j))^b$, $b{=}1$, cap $r_{\max}{=}3$), (iv)~\textbf{graduated} (exponential decay $w = \exp(-\alpha \cdot \hat{d})$, $\alpha \in \{0.1,\ldots,0.9\}$), (v)~\textbf{surprisal} (retain documents above corpus median surprisal), and (vi)~\textbf{DSIR}~\citep{xie2023dsir} (importance resampling against depth-0 reference).
6	
7	We fine-tune Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via LoRA (rank~8, $\alpha_{\text{LoRA}}{=}16$) for 3 epochs, evaluating on MMLU (14{,}042 examples, 0-shot) and HellaSwag (10{,}042 examples, 0-shot) across 5 seeds; the graduated strategy is further crossed with 5~$\alpha$ values (51 total runs).
8	
9	\paragraph{Results.}
10	
11	\begin{table}[t]
12	\centering
13	\small
14	\caption{Downstream performance of six data filtering strategies. Fine-tuning: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, LoRA, 30K documents, 5 seeds. Graduated shows best $\alpha$ only; full sweep in Table~\ref{tab:tab_alpha_sweep}.}
15	\label{tab:tab_filtering_main}
16	\input{tables/tab_filtering_main}
17	\end{table}
18	
19	All strategies degrade absolute performance relative to the base model (MMLU 0.6018, HellaSwag 0.6821); the goal is damage minimization rather than improvement.
20	Binary-ours minimizes degradation most effectively (MMLU $0.5941 \pm 0.0008$; HellaSwag $0.6701 \pm 0.0006$), reducing the MMLU gap from $-$1.53\,pp (no-filter) to $-$0.77\,pp.
21	Binary-Drayson ($0.5913$; $0.6691$) and graduated filtering at its best $\alpha$ both fall short of binary-ours.
22	Surprisal-based selection (MMLU $0.5894 \pm 0.0009$; HellaSwag $0.6641 \pm 0.0006$) falls short by $-$0.47\,pp / $-$0.60\,pp.
23	DSIR performs worst among all strategies (MMLU $0.5869 \pm 0.0003$; HellaSwag $0.6631 \pm 0.0007$), only $+$0.04\,pp above no-filter on MMLU and $-$0.07\,pp below on HellaSwag---its bigram feature hashing captures domain shift but not the depth-correlated distributional signatures that our classifier exploits.
24	
25	\paragraph{$\alpha$ sensitivity.}
26	Higher $\alpha$ values yield monotonically better performance on both benchmarks (HellaSwag: $0.6640$ at $\alpha{=}0.1$ to $0.6701$ at $\alpha{=}0.9$).
27	At $\alpha{=}0.9$, graduated filtering narrows the MMLU gap to 0.49\,pp below binary-ours ($0.5892$ vs.\ $0.5941$) and matches binary-ours exactly on HellaSwag ($0.6701$)---consistent with higher $\alpha$ progressively approximating binary thresholding.
28	The fact that even the best graduated configuration does not reach binary-ours confirms that ordinal depth assignments for $d \geq 2$ introduce noise rather than signal (detailed $\alpha$ sweep in Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
29	
30	\paragraph{Summary.}
31	$\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts the strategy ordering: binary curation at the $\Kempirical$ boundary minimizes degradation most effectively, while finer-grained strategies (ordinal depth weighting, surprisal scoring, DSIR) provide no additional benefit---consistent with depth assignments beyond $k{=}2$ carrying no discriminative signal.
32

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	\paragraph{Interpretation.}
5	The consistency of $\Kempirical = 2$ at $\theta{=}0.60$ across all tested configurations (4 model-mode and 4 decoding strategies) indicates that the two-step information bottleneck is a structural feature of autoregressive generation at the $\leq$1.5B scale.
6	The feature degradation analysis provides mechanistic evidence: surprisal-variance features degrade in a shared order across model families (Spearman $\rho \geq 0.85$), suggesting that each generation step smooths the token-level surprisal landscape in a model-independent fashion.
7	Cross-model neural probing reveals that $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$ for Qwen-continuation but $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 2$ for Pythia and OLMo; the Qwen elevation likely reflects self-familiarity artifacts in instruction-tuned embeddings rather than a universal signal, so $\Ktheory \geq 3$ can only be claimed for Qwen representations (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_neural_probe}).
8	Extended theoretical discussion, including connections to model collapse theory and scale considerations, appears in Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion}.
9	
10	\paragraph{Practical implications.}
11	The implied three-tier taxonomy (human / generation-1 / generation-2+) requires no per-model or per-decoding-strategy calibration.
12	Cross-model transfer (80--92\% accuracy retention; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}) enables deployment without generator-specific retraining.
13	Our filtering experiments (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}) show that binary filtering at the $\Kempirical{=}2$ boundary is the most effective strategy among those tested; graduated strategies offer no additional benefit.
14	Frontier LLMs achieve ${\sim}88\%$ binary detection (GPT-5.5: 87.8\%; Claude Opus~4.6: 88.2\%) but only ${\sim}33\%$ five-class depth accuracy (below OBD's 38.6\%), confirming that depth estimation is not solved by frontier LLMs in a zero-shot setting (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_llm}); few-shot or fine-tuned LLMs may narrow this gap.
15	
16

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We presented the first systematic measurement of the generational depth discrimination boundary $\Kempirical$ for recursive synthetic text.
5	At $\theta = 0.60$ (Cohen's $h \approx 0.20$), $\Kempirical = 2$ across 4 model-mode configurations and a decoding ablation covering 4 strategies at the $\leq$1.5B scale: all 1v2 bootstrap CI lower bounds exceed $\theta$ (permutation $p \leq 0.002$) while all 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below it.
6	Cross-model transfer retains 80--92\% accuracy when features are computed by a fixed scorer, with 0v1 $\auc > 0.96$ across all pairs.
7	Neural probing yields $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$ for Qwen-continuation but $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 2$ for Pythia and OLMo, establishing $\Kempirical = 2$ as a feature-set-specific lower bound; the Qwen elevation reflects self-familiarity rather than a universal depth signal.
8	
9	The $\Kempirical = 2$ boundary correctly predicts the strategy ordering in downstream filtering: binary curation minimizes degradation most effectively among all tested strategies, while all approaches (including binary-ours at $0.5941$ MMLU) remain below the base model ($0.6018$).
10	
11	Key directions for future work include scaling to 7B+ models, extending to multilingual and multi-domain corpora, establishing the prompt-chain vs.\ retrain-chain $\Kstar$ relationship, and developing model-agnostic neural probes that overcome the self-familiarity limitation.
12

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We presented the first systematic measurement of the generational depth discrimination boundary $\Kempirical$ for recursive synthetic text.
At $\theta = 0.60$ (Cohen's $h \approx 0.20$), $\Kempirical = 2$ across 4 model-mode configurations and a decoding ablation covering 4 strategies at the $\leq$1.5B scale: all 1v2 bootstrap CI lower bounds exceed $\theta$ (permutation $p \leq 0.002$) while all 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below it.
Cross-model transfer retains 80--92\% accuracy when features are computed by a fixed scorer, with 0v1 $\auc > 0.96$ across all pairs.
Neural probing yields $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$ for Qwen-continuation but $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 2$ for Pythia and OLMo, establishing $\Kempirical = 2$ as a feature-set-specific lower bound; the Qwen elevation reflects self-familiarity rather than a universal depth signal.

The $\Kempirical = 2$ boundary correctly predicts the strategy ordering in downstream filtering: binary curation minimizes degradation most effectively among all tested strategies, while all approaches (including binary-ours at $0.5941$ MMLU) remain below the base model ($0.6018$).

Key directions for future work include scaling to 7B+ models, extending to multilingual and multi-domain corpora, establishing the prompt-chain vs.\ retrain-chain $\Kstar$ relationship, and developing model-agnostic neural probes that overcome the self-familiarity limitation.

1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related_work}
3	
4	\paragraph{Model Collapse.}
5	Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} showed that iterative training on model outputs causes irreversible tail-distribution degradation.
6	Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point, and Dohmatob et al.~\cite{dohmatob2024model} derived scaling laws for tail probability loss.
7	Schaeffer et al.~\cite{schaeffer2025position} organized the literature into eight definitions; our $\Kstar$ aligns with their Family~B (D4: collapsing variance, D6: mode entanglement).
8	Kazdan et al.~\cite{kazdan2025collapse} distinguished replace and accumulate regimes; our prompt-chain operates in the replace regime, making $\Kempirical = 2$ a conservative lower bound.
9	These works characterize macro dynamics but provide no per-text depth estimation tools.
10	
11	\paragraph{Binary Synthetic Text Detection.}
12	Detection methods---DetectGPT~\cite{mitchell2023detectgpt}, Fast-DetectGPT~\citep{bao2024fast}, Binoculars~\cite{hans2024binoculars}, DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye}, Min-K\%++~\cite{zhang2024minkpp}, CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec}---achieve strong human-vs.-machine separation but produce no depth estimate.
13	DivEye's surprisal diversity features overlap with our \texttt{surp\_*} subset, but optimize for binary detection rather than ordinal depth discrimination.
14	Sadasivan et al.~\cite{sadasivan2023detect} showed theoretical limits of binary detection under paraphrasing; Krishna et al.~\cite{krishna2023paraphrasing} demonstrated that paraphrasing evades detectors while retrieval provides a defense---relevant to our rewrite-mode analysis.
15	Hao et al.~\cite{hao2025rewrite} addressed rewrite-mode transfer for binary detection.
16	Recent work moves beyond binary labels along other axes: collaboration degree~\cite{cheng2025beyond} and contamination type hierarchies~\cite{mehta2025beyond}, but neither addresses recursive generation depth.
17	
18	\paragraph{Data Selection.}
19	DSIR~\cite{xie2023dsir}, D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4}, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} improve corpus quality through distribution matching but ignore recursive depth.
20	Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025} combined binary detection with stratified importance resampling---a special case of our framework when $\Kstar = 1$.
21	Feng et al.~\cite{feng2025beyond} showed external verification can prevent collapse; our $\Kstar$ can inform such verifiers by delineating the depth frontier below which quality discrimination remains feasible.
22	
23	\paragraph{Ordinal Classification and Probing.}
24	Ordinal regression~\cite{frank2001ordinal, cao2020coral} exploits label ordering but has not been applied to synthetic text depth.
25	Our OBD head follows Frank \& Hall's binary decomposition principle.
26	Probing classifiers~\cite{alain2017understanding, conneau2018probing, belinkov2022probing} analyze pretrained representations; our neural probe follows this protocol with a controlled-capacity MLP on frozen embeddings.
27

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related_work}

\paragraph{Model Collapse.}
Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} showed that iterative training on model outputs causes irreversible tail-distribution degradation.
Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point, and Dohmatob et al.~\cite{dohmatob2024model} derived scaling laws for tail probability loss.
Schaeffer et al.~\cite{schaeffer2025position} organized the literature into eight definitions; our $\Kstar$ aligns with their Family~B (D4: collapsing variance, D6: mode entanglement).
Kazdan et al.~\cite{kazdan2025collapse} distinguished replace and accumulate regimes; our prompt-chain operates in the replace regime, making $\Kempirical = 2$ a conservative lower bound.
These works characterize macro dynamics but provide no per-text depth estimation tools.

\paragraph{Binary Synthetic Text Detection.}
Detection methods---DetectGPT~\cite{mitchell2023detectgpt}, Fast-DetectGPT~\citep{bao2024fast}, Binoculars~\cite{hans2024binoculars}, DivEye~\cite{basani2026diveye}, Min-K\%++~\cite{zhang2024minkpp}, CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec}---achieve strong human-vs.-machine separation but produce no depth estimate.
DivEye's surprisal diversity features overlap with our \texttt{surp\_*} subset, but optimize for binary detection rather than ordinal depth discrimination.
Sadasivan et al.~\cite{sadasivan2023detect} showed theoretical limits of binary detection under paraphrasing; Krishna et al.~\cite{krishna2023paraphrasing} demonstrated that paraphrasing evades detectors while retrieval provides a defense---relevant to our rewrite-mode analysis.
Hao et al.~\cite{hao2025rewrite} addressed rewrite-mode transfer for binary detection.
Recent work moves beyond binary labels along other axes: collaboration degree~\cite{cheng2025beyond} and contamination type hierarchies~\cite{mehta2025beyond}, but neither addresses recursive generation depth.

\paragraph{Data Selection.}
DSIR~\cite{xie2023dsir}, D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4}, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} improve corpus quality through distribution matching but ignore recursive depth.
Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025} combined binary detection with stratified importance resampling---a special case of our framework when $\Kstar = 1$.
Feng et al.~\cite{feng2025beyond} showed external verification can prevent collapse; our $\Kstar$ can inform such verifiers by delineating the depth frontier below which quality discrimination remains feasible.

\paragraph{Ordinal Classification and Probing.}
Ordinal regression~\cite{frank2001ordinal, cao2020coral} exploits label ordering but has not been applied to synthetic text depth.
Our OBD head follows Frank \& Hall's binary decomposition principle.
Probing classifiers~\cite{alain2017understanding, conneau2018probing, belinkov2022probing} analyze pretrained representations; our neural probe follows this protocol with a controlled-capacity MLP on frozen embeddings.

1	\section{Extended Discussion}
2	\label{sec:extended_discussion}
3	
4	\subsection{Theoretical Implications of $\Kempirical = 2$}
5	
6	The Data Processing Inequality guarantees the existence of a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).
7	Our empirical result---$\Kempirical = 2$ consistently across all 8 tested configurations---establishes that this boundary is remarkably shallow at the $\leq$1.5B scale.
8	
9	The shallowness is explained by the rate of information loss.
10	The 0v1 boundary is near-trivially separable ($\auc > 0.99$), reflecting the large distributional gap between human and first-generation text.
11	At 1v2, $\auc$ drops by ${\sim}$30\,pp (range: 0.6112--0.7039 across all conditions), indicating that the majority of discriminative signal is consumed in the first generation step.
12	By 2v3, $\auc$ falls to 0.5496--0.5917---below $\theta = 0.60$---and deeper pairs converge toward chance.
13	
14	This pattern aligns with model collapse findings.
15	Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} observed that tail-distribution degradation is most acute in the earliest generations.
16	Dohmatob et al.~\cite{dohmatob2024model} derived scaling laws demonstrating predictable tail probability mass loss.
17	Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point; $\Kempirical = 2$ indicates that operationally, this approach is rapid enough that adjacent-generation distinctions collapse within two steps.
18	
19	The consistency across decoding strategies merits emphasis.
20	Greedy, nucleus ($p{=}0.9$), $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$ all yield $\Kempirical = 2$ (Table~\ref{tab:s2_decoding}), with 1v2 $\auc$ in $[0.6866, 0.7039]$.
21	Higher decoding entropy modestly increases signal strength but does not shift the boundary, suggesting that $\Kempirical$ is governed by the information bottleneck of the generation process rather than sampling algorithm properties.
22	
23	\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer Implications}
24	
25	The cross-model transfer results (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}) indicate that depth signals are largely encoded in text-level statistical properties rather than generator-specific artifacts.
26	Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo retains 90--92\% accuracy, and broader continuation-mode transfer shows 80--92\% retention across all pairs.
27	At 0v1, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 for all pairs, confirming fully transferable binary contamination detection.
28	
29	A single depth classifier trained on one model's outputs can be deployed for texts from other models without retraining---extending utility to open-web settings where the generating model is unknown.
30	
31	Two caveats: (1)~a nontrivial model-specific residual persists despite high transfer, and (2)~Qwen-continuation$\leftrightarrow$OLMo retention (80--85\%) is lower than Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo (90--92\%), indicating that model family similarity modulates transfer even among continuation-mode configurations.
32	
33	\subsection{Feature Importance Across Decoding Strategies}
34	
35	While $\Kempirical = 2$ is consistent across decoding strategies, feature importance ordering varies.
36	Greedy and $T{=}0.7$ share highly correlated rankings (Spearman $\rho = 0.914$), with vocabulary diversity measures dominating.
37	Greedy versus $T{=}1.2$ yields lower correlation ($\rho = 0.53$, $p = 0.041$; suggestive but nonsignificant after Bonferroni correction).
38	$T{=}1.2$ promotes \texttt{hapax\_ratio}, \texttt{ttr}, and \texttt{surp\_skew} to top ranks; \texttt{freq\_entropy} rises from rank~10 (greedy) to rank~5.
39	
40	The \emph{existence} of the depth boundary is robust, but the \emph{optimal feature subset} depends on sampling strategy.
41	A general-purpose classifier should incorporate features from multiple groups.
42	
43	\subsection{Scale Considerations}
44	
45	Our $\Kempirical = 2$ at $\leq$1.5B constitutes a methodological lower bound.
46	All 15 features are computed from surface-level token statistics without model internals, and cross-model transfer (80--92\%) demonstrates methodology generalization across architectures.
47	
48	Scaling to larger models presents two outcomes: if $\Kempirical > 2$ at 7B+ (as scaling laws suggest~\cite{dohmatob2024model}), depth contamination becomes more insidious and our framework more necessary; if $\Kempirical = 2$ persists, our conclusions generalize directly.
49	The high cross-model transfer across three architecturally distinct families provides indirect evidence that depth signals are not tied to a specific pretraining paradigm.
50	
51	\subsection{Cross-Model Neural Probe Analysis}
52	\label{sec:extended_neural_probe}
53	
54	The neural probe (frozen-encoder MLP on each model's own hidden states) yields model-dependent $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}}$: Qwen-continuation achieves 2v3 $\auc = 0.6159$ $[0.610, 0.622]$, exceeding $\theta$ for $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$; Pythia-1.4B ($\auc_{2v3} = 0.5963$ $[0.589, 0.603]$) and OLMo-1B ($\auc_{2v3} = 0.5892$ $[0.582, 0.597]$) both fall below $\theta$, matching the 15D boundary at $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 2$.
55	
56	The Qwen-only elevation is consistent with a \emph{self-familiarity} effect: each probe uses the generator's own frozen embeddings to classify its own outputs.
57	Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, as an instruction-tuned model, encodes richer mode-specific artifacts in its hidden states that enable finer depth discrimination---but these artifacts do not transfer across model families.
58	By contrast, the 15D hand-crafted features yield $\Kempirical = 2$ universally across all three models, confirming that model-free statistical features provide a more robust and transferable depth signal.
59

\section{Extended Discussion}
\label{sec:extended_discussion}

\subsection{Theoretical Implications of $\Kempirical = 2$}

The Data Processing Inequality guarantees the existence of a finite $\Ktheory$ beyond which adjacent generations become indistinguishable (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).
Our empirical result---$\Kempirical = 2$ consistently across all 8 tested configurations---establishes that this boundary is remarkably shallow at the $\leq$1.5B scale.

The shallowness is explained by the rate of information loss.
The 0v1 boundary is near-trivially separable ($\auc > 0.99$), reflecting the large distributional gap between human and first-generation text.
At 1v2, $\auc$ drops by ${\sim}$30\,pp (range: 0.6112--0.7039 across all conditions), indicating that the majority of discriminative signal is consumed in the first generation step.
By 2v3, $\auc$ falls to 0.5496--0.5917---below $\theta = 0.60$---and deeper pairs converge toward chance.

This pattern aligns with model collapse findings.
Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024collapse} observed that tail-distribution degradation is most acute in the earliest generations.
Dohmatob et al.~\cite{dohmatob2024model} derived scaling laws demonstrating predictable tail probability mass loss.
Alemohammad et al.~\cite{alemohammad2024selfconsuming} proved convergence to a fixed point; $\Kempirical = 2$ indicates that operationally, this approach is rapid enough that adjacent-generation distinctions collapse within two steps.

The consistency across decoding strategies merits emphasis.
Greedy, nucleus ($p{=}0.9$), $T{=}0.7$, and $T{=}1.2$ all yield $\Kempirical = 2$ (Table~\ref{tab:s2_decoding}), with 1v2 $\auc$ in $[0.6866, 0.7039]$.
Higher decoding entropy modestly increases signal strength but does not shift the boundary, suggesting that $\Kempirical$ is governed by the information bottleneck of the generation process rather than sampling algorithm properties.

\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer Implications}

The cross-model transfer results (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}) indicate that depth signals are largely encoded in text-level statistical properties rather than generator-specific artifacts.
Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo retains 90--92\% accuracy, and broader continuation-mode transfer shows 80--92\% retention across all pairs.
At 0v1, cross-model $\auc$ exceeds 0.96 for all pairs, confirming fully transferable binary contamination detection.

A single depth classifier trained on one model's outputs can be deployed for texts from other models without retraining---extending utility to open-web settings where the generating model is unknown.

Two caveats: (1)~a nontrivial model-specific residual persists despite high transfer, and (2)~Qwen-continuation$\leftrightarrow$OLMo retention (80--85\%) is lower than Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo (90--92\%), indicating that model family similarity modulates transfer even among continuation-mode configurations.

\subsection{Feature Importance Across Decoding Strategies}

While $\Kempirical = 2$ is consistent across decoding strategies, feature importance ordering varies.
Greedy and $T{=}0.7$ share highly correlated rankings (Spearman $\rho = 0.914$), with vocabulary diversity measures dominating.
Greedy versus $T{=}1.2$ yields lower correlation ($\rho = 0.53$, $p = 0.041$; suggestive but nonsignificant after Bonferroni correction).
$T{=}1.2$ promotes \texttt{hapax\_ratio}, \texttt{ttr}, and \texttt{surp\_skew} to top ranks; \texttt{freq\_entropy} rises from rank~10 (greedy) to rank~5.

The \emph{existence} of the depth boundary is robust, but the \emph{optimal feature subset} depends on sampling strategy.
A general-purpose classifier should incorporate features from multiple groups.

\subsection{Scale Considerations}

Our $\Kempirical = 2$ at $\leq$1.5B constitutes a methodological lower bound.
All 15 features are computed from surface-level token statistics without model internals, and cross-model transfer (80--92\%) demonstrates methodology generalization across architectures.

Scaling to larger models presents two outcomes: if $\Kempirical > 2$ at 7B+ (as scaling laws suggest~\cite{dohmatob2024model}), depth contamination becomes more insidious and our framework more necessary; if $\Kempirical = 2$ persists, our conclusions generalize directly.
The high cross-model transfer across three architecturally distinct families provides indirect evidence that depth signals are not tied to a specific pretraining paradigm.

\subsection{Cross-Model Neural Probe Analysis}
\label{sec:extended_neural_probe}

The neural probe (frozen-encoder MLP on each model's own hidden states) yields model-dependent $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}}$: Qwen-continuation achieves 2v3 $\auc = 0.6159$ $[0.610, 0.622]$, exceeding $\theta$ for $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 3$; Pythia-1.4B ($\auc_{2v3} = 0.5963$ $[0.589, 0.603]$) and OLMo-1B ($\auc_{2v3} = 0.5892$ $[0.582, 0.597]$) both fall below $\theta$, matching the 15D boundary at $\Kempirical^{\text{neural}} = 2$.

The Qwen-only elevation is consistent with a \emph{self-familiarity} effect: each probe uses the generator's own frozen embeddings to classify its own outputs.
Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, as an instruction-tuned model, encodes richer mode-specific artifacts in its hidden states that enable finer depth discrimination---but these artifacts do not transfer across model families.
By contrast, the 15D hand-crafted features yield $\Kempirical = 2$ universally across all three models, confirming that model-free statistical features provide a more robust and transferable depth signal.

This result strengthens the practical case for model-free features: $\Ktheory \geq 3$ can only be claimed for Qwen representations specifically, while the model-free $\Kempirical = 2$ boundary holds as a feature-set-specific lower bound across all tested architectures.

\subsection{LLM Zero-Shot Baseline}
\label{sec:extended_llm}

On a 500-sample test set (5 depth classes), GPT-5.5 achieves 33.2\% accuracy (MAE = 1.10) and Claude Opus~4.6 achieves 33.1\% (MAE = 1.15)---both below OBD-LightGBM's 38.6\% (Table~\ref{tab:s3_llm_zeroshot}).
Both achieve ${\sim}$88\% binary accuracy.

Per-depth analysis: both models achieve high depth-0 recall (GPT-5.5: 0.77, Claude: 0.69) but recall for depths 1--4 collapses to 0.08--0.38, with predictions scattered nearly uniformly across non-human classes.
Spearman correlations are weak ($\rho = 0.38$, $0.42$), confirming that frontier LLMs function as binary detectors augmented by near-random depth guessing.

Statistical detection methods (DetectGPT~\cite{mitchell2023detectgpt}, Binoculars~\cite{hans2024binoculars}) optimize scalar scores for the binary boundary---the same distinction where LLM baselines excel.
But the per-depth recall collapse demonstrates that binary detection confidence is orthogonal to generational depth.

\subsection{Broader Impact}

The practical consequence of $\Kempirical = 2$ is a three-tier taxonomy: human-authored (depth~0), first-generation synthetic (depth~1), and deeper synthetic (depth~$\geq 2$).
A single round of synthetic rewriting suffices to make text statistically indistinguishable from multiply recycled text---a one-wash laundering effect that limits filtering granularity.

$\Kstar$ provides a corpus audit metric: what fraction of a training corpus consists of depth-$\geq 2$ text?
If prompt-chain depth signals serve as an observable proxy for early-stage model collapse, depth estimation could provide a lightweight diagnostic without expensive retraining experiments.

\subsection{Degradation and Practical Considerations}

In our continual training experiments (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}), all strategies degrade the base model's general capabilities (MMLU: 0.6018 $\to$ 0.5865--0.5941; HellaSwag: 0.6821 $\to$ 0.6638--0.6701).
This must be interpreted in context: our 100\% synthetic setting provides an upper-bound characterization.
In realistic mixed-corpus settings, degradation is proportional to the contamination fraction~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
Even under this extreme condition, $\Kstar$-aware binary filtering reduces MMLU degradation from $-$1.53\,pp to $-$0.77\,pp---an approximately 50\% reduction.

Binary filtering at the $\Kstar = 2$ boundary requires no per-model calibration, is simple to implement, and is universally applicable across tested generator configurations.
Combining depth-aware filtering with distribution-matching methods (DSIR, DoReMi) is a promising direction.

\subsection{Extended Limitations}
\label{sec:extended_limitations}

\emph{Prompt-chain versus retrain-chain.}
Our prompt-chain protocol holds model quality constant; real-world retrain-chains introduce additional degradation through training dynamics.
Under the monotonic-degradation assumption~\cite{shumailov2024collapse}, $\Kstar^{\text{retrain}} \leq \Kstar^{\text{prompt}}$, making our $\Kempirical = 2$ a conservative estimate.

\emph{Threshold sensitivity.}
At $\theta = 0.55$, $\Kempirical = 3$ uniformly.
At $\theta = 0.65$, continuation-mode configurations drop to $\Kempirical = 1$ while rewrite retains $\Kempirical = 2$.
At $\theta = 0.70$, $\Kempirical = 1$ universally.
The boundary is robust within a practical range but not invariant.

\emph{Boundary marginality.}
Qwen-continuation's 1v2 CI lower bound (0.6015) exceeds $\theta$ by only 0.15\,pp; Qwen-rewrite's 2v3 CI upper bound (0.5991) falls below $\theta$ by 0.09\,pp.
All eight boundary comparisons yield permutation $p < 0.01$.

\emph{Graduated filtering.}
Graduated filtering at all tested $\alpha$ values (0.1--0.9) underperforms binary-ours on MMLU (best: $0.5892$ at $\alpha{=}0.9$ vs.\ $0.5941$), with a monotonic trend.
At $\alpha{=}0.9$, HellaSwag matches binary-ours exactly ($0.6701$), consistent with $\Kempirical = 2$ predicting no benefit from finer ordinal structure.

\centering
\small
\caption{Graduated filtering $\alpha$ sweep (5 seeds, mean $\pm$ std). Higher $\alpha$ monotonically improves both benchmarks, converging toward binary-ours at $\alpha{=}0.9$.}
\label{tab:tab_alpha_sweep}
